{{Quote|Recitation: For example, on Praven Prime, the simple transferring of L'Xing syntax for 'friendship' changes its meaning&mdash;and implies that one's brood mate was actually impregnated by their own host.|HK-47|<ref name="KOTOR2" />}}
The '''L'Xing''' [[Language/Legends|language]] was spoken by the [[L'Xing]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Praven Prime]], situated in [[Gu-vandi]]-held [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. At some point by [[3951 BBY]], an [[HK-50 series assassin droid]] posing as a [[Translator droid/Legends|translator]] intentionally mistranslated an L'Xing phrase, which sparked a long [[Gu-vandi Collective–L'Xing civil war|civil war]] between the L'Xing and the [[Gu-vandi Collective]].

==Description==
[[File:PravenPrime-TEA.jpg|thumb|right|300px|L'Xing was spoken by a species that lived on Praven Prime.]]
L'Xing was a [[Language/Legends|language]] spoken by members of the [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[L'Xing]] [[Species/Legends|species]], who lived on the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Praven Prime]],<ref name="KOTOR2" /> a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Praven Prime system/Legends|Praven Prime system]]</ref> situated in [[Realspace/Legends|space]] controlled by the [[Gu-vandi]] species. According to the [[HK-series assassin droid]] [[HK-47]], the L'Xing had a "torpid" disposition that led them to favor words over actions.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

The concept of friendship could be expressed in the L'Xing language, as could an implication that a specific individual's [[Reproduction/Legends|brood]] mate had been impregnated by their own host. Furthermore, in spoken L'Xing the former idea could be switched to the latter via a simple syntax transfer respective to the language's equivalent of "friendship."<ref name="KOTOR2" />

==History==
{{Quote|Statement: This comment, of course, caused a civil war between the Gu-vandi Collective and L'Xing that still persists to the current date.|HK-47|<ref name="KOTOR2" />}}
At some point between [[3955 BBY]] and [[3951 BBY]],<ref name="Dates">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'', which establishes that the [[Gu-vandi Collective–L'Xing civil war|civil war]] between the [[Gu-vandi Collective]] and the [[L'Xing]] broke out no more than four [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior, to [[3951 BBY]].</ref> an [[HK-50 series assassin droid]]<ref name="KOTOR2" />&mdash;a unit of an [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droid]] model that had originally been designed by the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Revan/Legends|Darth Revan]] and that was later [[HK Manufacturing Plant|mass-produced]] by the rogue [[G0-T0 infrastructure planning system]] known as [[G0-T0]]<ref name="KOTORCG">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>&mdash;masquerading as a [[Translator droid/Legends|translator droid]] intentionally mistranslated the L'Xing word for "friendship." The translated comment caused a [[Gu-vandi Collective–L'Xing civil war|civil war]] between the L'Xing and the [[Gu-vandi Collective]].<ref name="KOTOR2" />

{{GameLSmechanics|Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords}}
In 3951 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="Dates" /> while the civil war was still ongoing, HK-47,<ref name="KOTOR2" /> who could communicate in more than six thousand forms of communication and had originally served as the basis for the HK-50 model,<ref name="KOTORCG" /> informed the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] known as the [[Meetra Surik|Jedi Exile]] about the role the L'Xing language played in the breakout of the conflict.<ref name="KOTOR2" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|If that was spoken aloud, then it would explain much&mdash;is that what happened?''"<br />"''Confirmation: Oh, truly. You can imagine the results.|A possible dialogue exchange between Mical and HK-47 in ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords''|<ref name="KOTOR2" />}}
[[File:HK-47.png|thumb|right|245px|In ''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'', L'Xing is mentioned in a dialogue with HK-47 (pictured).]]
The L'Xing language was introduced in the [[2004]] [[Obsidian Entertainment]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''. In the game, the language can be mentioned in an optional conversation the player character, the Jedi Exile, can have with the character HK-47. The Jedi Exile can state that they can imagine the consequences of the mistranslated L'Xing phrase, or they can profess a relative lack of knowledge of [[Alien/Legends|alien]] cultural studies and ask for HK-47 to elaborate.<ref name="KOTOR2" />

Alternatively, if the companion characters [[Mical]], [[Atton Rand]], or [[Brianna]] are present, Mical relays his understanding of the impact of the mistranslation while Rand and Brianna express their disbelief at the phrase having been spoken out loud and spoken directly to the individual targeted by the comment, respectively. This article assumes one hundred percent game completion and that the conversation took place as described.<ref name="KOTOR2" />
